subject: Human Evolution
title: High-Altitude Adaptations
description: A fast breakdown of High-Altitude Adaptations for builders.

hook.text: At 4,000 meters, oxygen drops 40%. Most people gasp. Tibetans breathe easy—their blood is different.

buildup.text: Living at extreme altitude causes altitude sickness, reduced fertility, and infant mortality in lowlanders.

discovery.text: Tibetans carry a variant of the EPAS1 gene that prevents dangerous overproduction of red blood cells.

twist.text: That gene variant came from Denisovans—an extinct human species that interbred with sapiens ancestors.

climax.text: A Denisovan gene, inherited tens of thousands of years ago, lets millions of Tibetans thrive today.

punchline.text: An extinct species gave Tibetans their lungs.

quiz.question: Where did the Tibetan high-altitude gene variant come from?
